title: Embeddings-first browser RAG playbook + lightweight agent shim (IndexedDB demo)
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide an intentionally minimal, privacy-conscious RAG reference that runs in the browser using an embeddings-first strategy. Many RAG quickstarts rely on server-side vector stores or heavy tool scaffolding; this PR demonstrates a different tradeoff: do light retrieval and filtering client-side (IndexedDB) and keep inference calls to Redwood minimal and deterministic.

What this PR adds: a new example playbook and a tiny TS agent shim that shows how to (1) build an embeddings-first retrieval pipeline in-browser, (2) implement deterministic tool-calling hooks for structured actions (evidence highlighting, link-out), and (3) wire Redwood API calls with streaming while preserving user privacy for local context. Includes a runnable demo (static HTML + wasm-friendly bundling) and docs pages in the handbook with UX and security guidance.

Highlights / design notes: - Embeddings-first: compute or fetch embeddings and store them in IndexedDB; retrieval does cosine search with approximate top-k then re-ranks by simple heuristic to keep latency under 50ms for small corpora. - Deterministic tool-calling: agent shim exposes a small schema and deterministic validation so the server-side decoder can be used in streaming mode without speculative side effects. - Offline/limited connectivity: demo demonstrates graceful degradation when API calls fail (cached answers, fallback to conservative summaries). - Security: guidance for public sites, advice to avoid embedding PII in local stores, and a pattern for ephemeral key rotation when using hosted Redwood.

Files changed include a new example directory (redwood-examples/browser-rag-embeddings-playbook/) and two handbook pages under redwood-docs. The demo is designed to be copy-paste runnable and includes a minimal build step (esbuild) and an optional wasm cosine-distance helper for larger corpora.

Checklist: - [x] Example code and README - [x] Demo HTML + minimal build scripts - [x] Handbook/guide + diagrams - [x] TS SDK sample wiring (browser-safe) - [x] Security section and suggested CSP/KMS patterns - [x] Unit tests for indexing + retrieval shim - [x] CI runs green (one flaky CI lint re-run required)

Related: ENG-3421 (embeddings-first experimentation), PM-118 (docs milestone). Not a breaking change.

How to run the demo locally: 1) cd redwood-examples/browser-rag-embeddings-playbook/demo 2) npm install && npm run build 3) serve -s dist 4) open http://localhost:5000 and follow onboarding to index a small corpus or pull sample embeddings.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the handbook language (clarity for product-facing engineers), the privacy guidance, and the deterministic tool schema shape (agent.ts). The shim and example are intentionally small — we want them to be safe to link-to from the docs site and usable as a starting point for partners building client-side augmentation flows.
